# Sley Agent Onboarding

Sley is an agent-native structural programming language. Source files are the
human review projection; the canonical working model is the typed graph exposed
by the Loom compiler.

Core commands:

```bash
cargo run -- check --json <file-or-project>
cargo run -- ast --json <file-or-project>
cargo run -- ast --json --node <node-id> <file-or-project>
cargo run -- graph --json <file-or-project>
cargo run -- graph --json --slice <node-id> <file-or-project>
cargo run -- new --json --template agent-project --name agent-app --module agent.main agent-app
cargo run -- doctor --json <file-or-project>
cargo run -- fix --json --kind add_module_declaration --dry-run <file-or-project>
cargo run -- fix --json --kind delete_unused_private_declarations --dry-run <file-or-project>
cargo run -- fix --json --kind delete_unused_private_declarations --write <file-or-project>
cargo run -- verify --json <file-or-project>
cargo run -- deploy --json --dry-run --artifacts-dir .sley/deploy <file-or-project>
cargo run --bin sley-ci -- lint --json --deny-warnings <file-or-project>
cargo run --bin sley-ci -- doctor --json --deny-warnings <file-or-project>
cargo run --bin sley-ci -- plan --json --graft-templates <file-or-project>
cargo run --bin sley-ci -- run --json <file-or-project>
cargo run --bin sley-ci -- deploy --json --dry-run --artifacts-dir .sley/ci-deploy <file-or-project>
cargo run --bin sley-ci -- corpus --json fixtures/corpus/manifest.json
cargo run --bin sley-ci -- examples --json examples
cargo run --bin sley-conformance -- report --json
cargo run --bin sley-conformance -- coverage --json --require-tag <tag>
cargo run --bin sley-contract -- inspect-deploy-artifacts .sley/deploy --schemas docs/schemas --json
make v1
make syntax
cargo run --bin sley-lsp
cargo run --bin sley-workbench -- --json --html .sley/workbench.html <file-or-project>
cargo run --bin sley-docgen -- reference --json --markdown .sley/reference.md <file-or-project>
cargo run --bin sley-agent-bench -- run --json
cargo run --bin sley-migrate -- report --json --schemas docs/schemas --fixtures fixtures/contracts <file-or-project>
cargo run --bin sley-sandbox-runner -- run --json <manifest.json>
cargo run --bin sley-zjx -- inspect --json <zjx-envelope.json>
cargo run --bin sley-zjx -- verify-digest --json <zjx-envelope.json>
cargo run -- seal --json <file-or-project>
cargo run -- graft --json --dry-run <file> <graft.json>
cargo run -- graft --json --write <file> <graft.json>
cargo run -- format <file>
cargo run -- run --json --cap DatabaseRead --db-table users=examples/users.json examples/db_gate.sley
cargo run -- run --json --cap DatabaseRead --cap DatabaseWrite --db-table users=examples/users.json examples/db_write_gate.sley
cargo run -- run --json --cap Network --http-text https://example.test/profile Ada examples/network_gate.sley
cargo run -- run --json --cap Shell --shell-output date 2026-05-05 examples/shell_gate.sley
cargo run -- run --json --cap ModelCall --model-output name Ada examples/model_gate.sley
cargo run -- run --json --cap SecretRead --secret api_key redacted examples/secret_gate.sley
cargo run -- run --json --cap Deploy --deploy-result staging staged examples/deploy_gate.sley
cargo run -- run --json --cap Spend --spend-result ads-budget authorized examples/spend_gate.sley
```

Agent rules:

- Prefer structural grafts over raw text edits.
- Run `check --json` after every proposed semantic change.
- Use `graph --json --slice <node-id>` before planning a bounded graft.
- Use `ast --json --node <node-id>` when exact task, statement, or expression
  shape matters; node reports use `schema: "sley.ast.node.v0"`.
- Treat diagnostic `repair_hints` as suggestions, not authority bypasses.
- For `PARSE_EXPECTED_*`, inspect `insert_expected_token`,
  `provide_identifier`, `provide_expression`, or `choose_expected_item` hints
  before guessing at syntax.
- For `GRAFT_PRECONDITION_FAILED`, inspect `refresh_graft_precondition` hints;
  stale grafts should be rebuilt from current AST/query state before retrying.
- For `GRAFT_MOVE_UNSUPPORTED` and `GRAFT_DELETE_UNSUPPORTED`, inspect
  `use_supported_graft_operation` hints before retrying; expression targets
  should normally switch to `ReplaceExpression` instead of move/delete.
- For duplicate declaration diagnostics and graft `*_EXISTS` namespace
  collisions, inspect `resolve_namespace_conflict`; choose a new name, remove
  the duplicate, or reuse the existing declaration instead of retrying.
- For `CALL_ARITY_MISMATCH`, prefer structural `update_call_args` or
  `remove_call_arg` hints when present; their replacements are starter
  `UpdateCallArgs` or `RemoveCallArg` graft JSON.
- For `CALL_ARGUMENT_TYPE_MISMATCH`, prefer the structural `replace_call_arg`
  hint when present; its replacement is caller-scoped starter
  `ReplaceCallArg` graft JSON.
- For binding or assignment type mismatches, prefer structural
  `replace_expression` graft JSON when the declared/local type should remain.
- For Bool condition, collection element, map key/value, index key, and
  record-field type diagnostics, prefer structural `replace_expression` graft
  JSON when the surrounding structure is correct and only the expression should
  change.
- For record literal missing/unknown field diagnostics, inspect the
  whole-record `replace_expression` graft JSON; it preserves known expected
  fields and removes unknown fields.
- For unary or binary operator type diagnostics, prefer structural
  `replace_expression` graft JSON when present; the checker omits it for
  ambiguous operator families.
- For `IF_BRANCH_TYPE_MISMATCH`, inspect both structural `replace_expression`
  graft JSON hints and choose the branch whose value should conform.
- For non-iterable `each` collections and invalid `len` arguments, treat
  structural `replace_expression` hints as conservative valid starters and
  refine the value after the graft checks.
- For `INDEX_COLLECTION_NOT_INDEXABLE`, prefer structural `replace_expression`
  hints when present; the checker chooses list or map starters from the index
  expression type.
- For `RETURN_TYPE_MISMATCH`, use `change_return_type` only when the signature
  should change; otherwise prefer structural `replace_expression` graft JSON.
- For `MISSING_RETURN`, add a guaranteed return path or use the
  `replace_task_body` starter; do not delete the last return from a non-`Unit`
  task.
- Do not add effects only to silence diagnostics; the authority must be real.
- Do not invent binding kinds. The stable vocabulary is in
  `docs/SleyLanguageSpec.md`.
- Keep formatting controlled by `sley format`.
- Do not use old names or old-project framing. This project is Sley.
- Current typed host fallibility includes filesystem reads/writes, seeded
  database reads, per-run `db.try_insert` writes, seeded `http.try_get_text`
  network text reads, seeded `shell.try_run` command output reads, and seeded
  `model.try_complete` prompt completions, plus seeded `secrets.try_get`
  secret values, seeded `deploy.try_stage` deployment stage results, and
  seeded `spend.try_authorize` spend authorization results.

- `sley.deploy.report.v0`

The graft outcome schema pins accepted provenance records with non-empty
targets and `result: "accepted"` and has a locked accepted-operation fixture.
The diagnostics schema exposes a shared diagnostic record used by graft,
doctor, plan, and verify report schemas.
The query schema exposes strict task, take, type, effect, and call summary row
definitions for downstream bindings.
The `sley-contract` binary exposes `inventory`, `check-fixtures`, `validate`,
and `inspect-deploy-artifacts` JSON Schema validation reports for
schema/fixture/manifest/deploy-handoff contract-kit work; inventory,
fixture-check, and validate reports have locked fixtures.
The `sley-ci` binary exposes `check`, `lint`, `doctor`, `plan`, `run`, `verify`, `deploy`, `smoke`, `corpus`, and `examples` reports
for local CI and pre-commit gates over existing Sley commands.
The `sley-conformance` binary exposes `report` and `coverage` JSON roots for
schema/fixture instance coverage, contract validation status, corpus tags,
smoke tags, packaged example counts, and declared integration-test count drift.
The in-tree `tree-sitter-sley` package exposes the current syntax grammar,
highlight queries, generated parser artifacts, exact corpus tests, and fixture
parsing smoke through `npm test` or `make syntax`.
The `sley-lsp` binary exposes stdio LSP diagnostics, formatting, document
symbols, declaration hover, edit-plan code actions, and non-mutating
`sley.fix.preview` payloads backed by compiler modules; the preview payload
uses `schema: "sley.lsp.fix_preview.v0"` and has a locked contract fixture.
The `sley-workbench` binary exposes `schema: "sley.workbench.report.v0"` and
optional static HTML over doctor/query/lint/plan/graph panels without source
file writes.
The `sley-docgen` binary exposes `schema: "sley.docgen.report.v0"` and
optional Markdown over checked module, task, type, effect, and capability
reference data.
The `sley-agent-bench` binary exposes
`schema: "sley.agent_bench.report.v0"` for deterministic local repair-loop
benchmarks over JSON inspection, checked fixes, post-fix gates, trace receipts,
seal digests, and ZJX handoff evidence.
The `sley-migrate` binary exposes `schema: "sley.migrate.report.v0"` for
checked source migration reports and optional schema/fixture drift checks.
The `sley-sandbox-runner` binary consumes
`schema: "sley.sandbox.manifest.v0"` manifests and emits
`schema: "sley.sandbox.report.v0"` for deterministic seeded runtime replays.
The `sley-zjx` binary exposes `schema: "sley.zjx.tool.report.v0"` for
read-only `inspect`, `verify-digest`, `extract-graph`, and `diff-envelope`
commands over `sley.zjx.envelope.v0` preview envelopes.
The repo-level `Makefile`, `.github/actions/sley-v1/action.yml`,
`.github/workflows/v1.yml`, and `.pre-commit-config.yaml` all route release
checks through `make v1`.
Graph-slice insert/move/delete/replace affordance operations reuse the strict
graft operation schema from edit-plan reports.
Graph-slice focus, optional task, and inbound/outbound call summaries reuse
AST and query report contracts.
The trace report schema wraps trace receipt JSONL records for `sley trace --json`;
the trace receipt schema pins each standalone JSONL record and references
accepted provenance records.
The ZJX envelope schema pins a recomputable `graph_digest`, references the
symbol graph, graph slice, and trace receipt schemas, and has a locked fixture
beside the full symbol graph fixture. The ZJX tool report schema pins local
inspection, digest verification, graph extraction, and envelope diff outputs.

Contract references:

- `docs/contracts.md`
- `docs/SleyLanguageSpec.md`
- `docs/schemas/*.schema.json`
- `fixtures/contracts/*.json`
- `fixtures/grafts/*.json`
- `tests/sley_v0.rs`
- `CHANGELOG.md`

Current development phase:

- typed host fallibility is in place for filesystem and seeded database
  adapters plus seeded network text, seeded shell output, seeded model
  completions, seeded secret values, seeded deployment stage results, and
  seeded spend authorization results through explicit fallible calls returning
  `Result<T, Error>`; database adapters can be narrowed with exact table
  scopes, while other non-file seeded adapters can be narrowed with
  `--cap EFFECT=SCOPE` deterministic text prefixes over the seeded resource
  key, and scope mismatches remain diagnostics
- release-readiness now includes manifest-backed CLI smokes for stable command
  output, JSON roots, graph/ZJX surfaces, run reports, edit-plan reports,
  deploy dry-run reports, graft/fix dry runs, strict edit-plan graft operation
  and transaction template schema envelopes, direct graft writes, temp setup
  files for write-mode smokes, explicit graft/fix trace receipts, non-empty
  trace receipt seals, ZJX envelopes carrying schema-backed trace receipts,
  ZJX tool reports, lint-driven fix writes that clear warnings before verify,
  and seeded host-adapter execution while preserving typed recoverable failure
  records and keeping authority failures as diagnostics
- checked graph query reports are available through `sley query --json` with
  root schema `sley.query.report.v0`; `--kind types` and `--kind effects`
  give direct declaration rows for record and authority surfaces, while
  `--kind calls` exposes strict call rows
- checked lint reports are available through `sley lint --json` with root schema
  `sley.lint.report.v0`; private-task rules include `unused_private_task` and
  `unreachable_private_task`, the authority hygiene rule
  `unused_declared_effect`, the import hygiene rule `unused_import`, the API
  hygiene rule `unused_take`, the declaration hygiene rules
  `unused_private_type` and `unused_private_effect`, and the migration rule
  `raw_host_adapter`, plus the style rules `missing_module_declaration` and
  `unqualified_imported_call`, the local cleanup rule
  `unused_pure_binding`, the no-op expression cleanup rule
  `unused_pure_expression_statement`, the mutable-local style rule
  `mutable_binding_never_set`, the self-assignment cleanup rule
  `self_assignment_statement`, the overwritten-set cleanup rule
  `overwritten_set_statement`, the redundant-initial-set cleanup rule
  `redundant_initial_set_statement`, the expression simplification rule
  `constant_if_expression`, the constant-if statement simplification rule
  `constant_if_statement`, the constant-false if cleanup rule
  `constant_false_if_statement`, the constant-false while cleanup rule
  `constant_false_while_statement`, the constant comparison simplification rule
  `constant_comparison_expression`, the constant arithmetic simplification rule
  `constant_arithmetic_expression`, the absorbing arithmetic simplification rule
  `absorbing_arithmetic_expression`, the constant text concatenation rule
  `constant_text_concatenation_expression`, the constant list index rule
  `constant_list_index_expression`, the constant map index rule
  `constant_map_index_expression`, the constant record field access rule
  `constant_record_field_access_expression`, the constant len rule
  `constant_len_expression`, the constant not rule
  `constant_not_expression`, the empty-if cleanup rule
  `empty_if_statement`, the empty-for cleanup rule
  `empty_for_statement`, the empty-forge cleanup rule
  `empty_forge_statement`, the identity simplification rule
  `identity_binary_expression` including empty-text concatenation, the
  redundant boolean comparison rule
  `redundant_boolean_comparison`, the absorbing boolean expression rule
  `absorbing_boolean_expression`, the idempotent boolean expression rule
  `idempotent_boolean_expression`, the self-comparison expression rule
  `self_comparison_expression` including strict and non-strict ordering, the
  double negation simplification rule
  `double_negation_expression`, the negated comparison simplification rule
  `negated_comparison_expression`, the redundant boolean-if simplification rule
  `redundant_boolean_if_expression`, the redundant boolean-if statement rule
  `redundant_boolean_if_statement`, the same-branch if simplification rules
  `same_branch_if_expression` and `same_branch_if_statement`, the dead-code
  cleanup rule `unreachable_statement`, and the result-safety rule
  `unchecked_result`
- `sley new --json` emits `sley.project.scaffold.v0` and creates
  non-destructive `hello`, `library`, `cli`, `service-gate`,
  `data-pipeline`, `deploy`, `spend-gate`, `agent`, `agent-task-pack`, or `agent-project`
  starter projects
  that can immediately run through check, doctor, query, plan, lint, local or
  seeded runtime gates with denied warnings, deploy dry-run packaging where
  applicable, seal, and ZJX handoff packaging; scaffold JSON includes typed
  `next_actions` plus legacy `next_commands`
- `sley doctor --json` emits `sley.doctor.report.v0` and consumes strict
  diagnostics plus checked query/lint summaries into one agent readiness report;
  call-bearing reports include `inspect_calls` next-actions for strict
  `sley query --kind calls` rows; warning reports include
  `plan_lint_repairs` next-actions that call
  `sley plan --json --graft-templates <target>` and `preview_lint_repair`
  next-actions with `sley fix --json --dry-run` when exactly one checked lint
  repair exists; these preview actions keep `command` non-mutating and include
  an explicit `write_command` for the matching `sley fix --write`. CLI smokes
  prove the previewed repair can be written and followed by clean
  `sley verify --json --deny-warnings` for both single-file and multi-file
  project targets, including generated deploy and agent scaffold quickstarts
  re-verified with seeded authority
- `sley plan --json` emits `sley.edit_plan.report.v0` and consumes strict
  diagnostics plus checked query/lint findings into ranked task edit surfaces,
  graft targets, call-row inspection next-actions, and post-edit gate commands;
  add `--graft-templates` to emit starter graft operation payloads,
  rename-plus-call-site transactions, and add-take-plus-call-arg transactions
  for the highest-ranked task surface, plus safe remove-take-plus-call-arg
  transactions when an unused take can be proven
  and lint-driven `DeleteNode` templates plus cleanup transactions for unused
  private type/effect declarations, plus `AddModuleDeclaration` templates for
  `missing_module_declaration` with module names inferred from the target file
  or project-relative path, plus `delete_unused_private_task` templates for
  dead private tasks, `delete_dead_private_tasks` cleanup transactions for
  dead private task groups and unreachable cycles, `remove_unused_take`
  templates for unused takes that validate through checked `RemoveTake`, and
  `remove_unused_declared_effect` templates for unused task-declared effects
  that validate through checked `RemoveTaskEffect`, and `delete_unused_import`
  templates for unused imports that validate through checked `DeleteNode`, plus
  `migrate_raw_host_adapter` templates for raw host calls that can safely move
  to fallible `try_` adapters with `?`, plus
  `propagate_unchecked_result` templates for discarded `Result` expression
  statements, plus `qualify_imported_call` templates for simple imported task
  calls that should be alias- or module-qualified, plus
  `delete_unused_pure_expression_statement` templates for no-op pure
  expression statements, plus
  `delete_self_assignment_statement` templates for no-op mutation statements,
  plus `delete_overwritten_set_statement` templates for dead set statements
  immediately overwritten before any read,
  plus `fold_redundant_initial_set_into_binding` and
  `convert_redundant_initial_set_to_bind` transactions for safe immediate
  mutable-initializer replacements,
  plus
  `delete_constant_false_if_statement` templates for never-executed
  `if false` statements without `else` branches, plus
  `delete_constant_false_while_statement` templates for never-executed
  `while false` statements, plus
  `simplify_constant_comparison_expression` templates for literal comparisons
  with constant boolean results, plus
  `simplify_constant_arithmetic_expression` templates for numeric literal
  arithmetic, plus
  `simplify_absorbing_arithmetic_expression` templates for delete-safe
  multiplication by zero, plus
  `simplify_constant_text_concatenation_expression` templates for text literal
  concatenation, plus
  `simplify_constant_list_index_expression` templates for literal list indexes,
  plus `simplify_constant_map_index_expression` templates for literal map
  indexes, plus `simplify_constant_record_field_access_expression` templates
  for literal record field access, plus `simplify_constant_len_expression`
  templates for literal `len` calls, plus
  `simplify_constant_not_expression` templates for literal boolean negation,
  plus
  `simplify_idempotent_boolean_expression` templates for delete-safe repeated
  boolean operands, plus
  `simplify_negated_comparison_expression` templates for inverted
  comparisons, plus
  `simplify_constant_if_statement` templates for constant `if` statements with
  one executing branch statement, plus
  `simplify_redundant_boolean_if_statement` templates for boolean `if`
  statements that can return the condition or its negation directly, plus
  `simplify_same_branch_if_statement` templates for same-branch statement-level
  `if` cleanup, plus
  `delete_empty_if_statement` templates for no-op `if` statements with
  delete-safe conditions and empty branches, plus
  `delete_empty_for_statement` templates for `for` statements over literal
  empty lists, plus
  `delete_empty_forge_statement` templates for no-op `forge { }` starter
  blocks, plus
  `delete_unreachable_statement` templates for dead statements after a
  guaranteed return, plus
  `convert_mutable_binding_to_bind` transactions for never-set mutable locals;
  selected task graph-slice
  affordances are surfaced as checked
  `move_statement`/`move_take`, destination-variant, `delete_statement`,
  `delete_take`, `replace_statement`, and `replace_expression` templates where
  legal, or
  `--template-surface <surface>` can target a specific task id, qualified task
  name, block node id, statement node id, take node id, expression node id, or
  lint finding node; selected task and block surfaces emit checked
  `insert_statement` starters, selected statement surfaces emit checked
  `replace_statement` starters, and the `program` surface emits checked
  `add_task`, `add_type_declaration`, `add_effect_declaration`, and
  `add_import` starters; `--emit-graft <kind>` prints one
  matching operation/transaction JSON object for `sley graft`
- `sley fix --json --kind <kind>` consumes checked plan templates and applies
  one named operation or transaction through the same graft checker, emitting
  `sley.graft.outcome.v0`; exact block, statement, take, and expression node
  surfaces can be selected with `--template-surface`; `--name <name>`,
  `--type <type>`, `--module <module>`, `--source <source>`,
  `--source-file <path>`, and
  `--position <n>` can override matching editable payload fields on
  single-operation templates before the normal graft checker runs; default and
  `--dry-run` mode are
  non-mutating, and `--write` records the normal graft trace receipt or a
  caller-supplied `--trace <trace.jsonl>` path; CLI smokes cover a call-row-driven
  `rename_and_update_call_sites` write and an unused-take
  `remove_take_and_remove_call_arg` write followed by call query and verify;
  `qualify_imported_call` write, call query, and strict verify for imported
  call style cleanup; `add_module_declaration` is the checked fixer for
  explicit module-declaration style warnings and uses the same module-name
  inference
- graft call-argument edits are structural: use `UpdateCallArgs` to insert,
  `ReplaceCallArg` to replace, and `RemoveCallArg` to remove checked caller
  arguments by task target plus optional `from`/`scope`
- `sley verify --json` emits `sley.verify.report.v0` and consumes strict
  diagnostics, checked query/lint summaries, and deterministic runtime
  execution into one CI/pre-deploy gate; scaffold templates include checked
  local pure starters, a seeded Network service smoke, a checked
  `--deny-warnings --cap Deploy --deploy-result staging staged` deploy smoke,
  a checked `--deny-warnings --cap Spend --spend-result ads-budget authorized`
  spend smoke,
  and seeded SecretRead/Network/ModelCall/Deploy agent smokes through both
  `sley verify` and `sley-ci verify`, direct runtime smoke through `sley run`
  and `sley-ci run`, plus deploy package smoke through `sley deploy` and
  `sley-ci deploy`; denied warning
  reports route agents to checked lint repair plans plus
  dry-run fix previews when the repair is unambiguous before deployment review;
  passed reports point agents to `sley seal --json <target>` and
  `sley zjx --json <target>` for review and handoff artifacts
- `sley run --json` emits `sley.run.report.v0` on successful deterministic
  execution, with the runtime value under `/value`
- `sley deploy --json --dry-run` emits `sley.deploy.report.v0` and composes
  strict verify, trace seal, and ZJX package summaries into one local deploy
  package report; it records `live_deploy_allowed=false`, makes no external
  mutations or provider calls, and keeps live deployment behind explicit
  operator approval. Add `--artifacts-dir <dir>` to write local
  `deploy-report.json`, `seal.json`, `zjx-envelope.json`, and digest-bearing
  `manifest.json` handoff files after the dry-run package is ready;
  `sley-ci deploy` passes the same flag through to the wrapped deploy command.
  Use `sley-contract inspect-deploy-artifacts <dir> --schemas docs/schemas
  --json` to validate the handoff manifest, schemas, and file digests after the
  directory moves between agent sessions
- `examples/agent_deploy_pipeline.sley` is the standalone dogfood path for
  SecretRead + Network + ModelCall + Deploy: check it, inspect it with
  doctor/query, lint with denied warnings, run with deterministic seeds, verify
  with denied warnings, then build and contract-inspect a local deploy dry-run
  package with optional artifact handoff files
- next development work should keep broadening style and migration lints after
  the empty-if cleanup path
- project graft writeback now supports create/update/delete module files,
  `AddImport` writes to existing on-disk module files that were not yet loaded
  through the entry import graph, and module rename, including manifest entry
  updates; top-level type/effect/task movement into known modules is supported,
  including AddImport-then-MoveNode transactions that create new module files
  from moved declarations; top-level import moves into known modules are
  supported for project writeback
- `MoveNode` supports cross-parent statement movement between existing block
  parents with `payload.destination`, take reordering within the owning task,
  and checked cross-task take movement into another task's take list; expression
  movement remains an explicit rejection, and expression move rejection carries
  a `replace_expression` repair hint
- graph, graph-slice, and query module import summaries expose canonical import
  node ids for graft targets such as `import:app.main:app.math`
- graph slices expose `insert_affordances` for task-local block
  `InsertStatement` planning, including exact block target ids, insertion
  limits, starter operation JSON, and editable JSON pointers
- graph slices expose `move_affordances` for bounded import/type/effect/task,
  statement, and take `MoveNode` planning, including exact parent ids,
  destination insertion limits, starter operation JSON, and editable JSON
  pointers
- graph slices expose `delete_affordances` for bounded
  import/type/effect/task/non-return statement/take `DeleteNode` planning;
  `sley plan --graft-templates` surfaces checked task-internal
  `delete_statement` and `delete_take` templates when the starter delete graft
  validates
- graph slices expose `replace_affordances` for task-local non-return
  `ReplaceStatement` and `ReplaceExpression` planning; `sley plan
  --graft-templates` surfaces checked `replace_statement` and
  `replace_expression` templates when the starter replace graft validates;
  direct statement surfaces can still emit checked no-op `ReplaceStatement`
  starters
- `sley plan --graft-templates --template-surface program` surfaces checked
  declaration starters for `add_task`, `add_type_declaration`, and
  `add_effect_declaration`; source-backed declaration starters can be executed
  through `sley fix --source` or `--source-file`, and name-backed starters can
  use `--name`
- manifest-backed accepted/rejected synthetic gold corpus growth, including
  spend and data helper boundaries for transitive authority checks
- broader graph-slice graft operations around insert/move/delete/replace planning
